text:
marta: Ran a targeted A100 vs H100 sweep this morning across us-west1 and eu-west1. Models: Llama2-7b, Mistral-7b, Mosaic-7b. Quant setups: q8 and q4f32. Batching: single-token prefill + decode (batch=1) and batch=8 steady-state.

marta: TL;DR numbers: H100 wins latency and tokens/sec consistently (example Llama2-7b prefill+decode p95: H100=42ms, A100=68ms). Tokens/sec (steady): H100~820 t/s, A100~520 t/s. Dollar math (our infra costs normalized): H100 ~$1.8 / 1M tokens, A100 ~$1.2 / 1M tokens for this workload. Caveat: A100 price-per-hour lower so cost ratio depends on utilization and batching.

marta: Notable: in eu-west1 A100 machines frequently hit a kernel fallthrough path for q4 on Mistral, causing p95 spikes ~2-3x. H100 had stable kernel selection. CSV + charts: s3://redwood-bench/1759004321/summary.csv and https://s3.console.aws/bench/1759004321/plots.png (internal).

jason: awesome. can you paste the exact runner command and kernel flags? want to repro the fallthrough locally.

marta: sure — minimal repro we used:```bash
./run_infer --model llama2-7b --device a100 --quant q4f32 --batch 1 --seq 1024 --kernel-policy auto --region eu-west1 --out csv
```

priya: quick note on quality: we ran 200 eval prompts (mix of instructions + code) — q4f32 produced a measurable drop vs fp16 on Llama2-7b: average pass@1 drop ~2.3%, a few hallucination cases flagged. q8 kept parity except on some long-context recall tests. Will add eval.csv in the bucket.

alex: for cost-to-quality tradeoffs, try: batch=4 with prefix-KV caching enabled and reduced kv eviction interval; that lifted tokens/sec on A100 by ~15% without raising p95. Also flip kernel-policy to prefer hopt kernels for decode path on A100 — reduced fallthroughs in our next run.

chris: did you try the H100 tensor-split kernel for Mosaic? we saw H100 + tensor-split + q4 gives best throughput on Mosaic-7b.

marta: yes — tensor-split + q4 on H100 gave the best tokens/sec for Mosaic (H100 ~910 t/s). But cost per 1M tokens still slightly higher than A100 at high-util because per-hour cost of H100 is higher; at high sustained QPS the throughput advantage pays off.

bench-bot: Automated summary uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/1759004321/auto_summary.json — highlights: kernel_fallback_count {"a100-eu-west1": 18, "h100-eu-west1": 2}, avg_token_latency_ms {"llama2-7b": {"h100": 1.22, "a100": 1.92}}.

jason: thanks. next steps: can we (1) run a focused batch=4 sweep on A100+kernel-policy=prefer-hopt in eu-west1, (2) run quality evals for the q4 cases with our 1k prompt regression set, and (3) annotate the cases where kernel fallback correlates with latency spike? I'll take point on (1).

marta: sounds good. I'll kick off (2) and (3) and drop the new CSVs into the same s3 prefix. ping here when you start the batch sweep. :rocket:

priya: adding a note to the eval dashboard to track q4 vs fp16 regressions over time — will create an alert if pass@1 drops >1.5% from baseline.

alex: FYI I left a short doc with kernel-policy guidance in the repo: https://internal.redwood/eng-ml/kernel-playbook.md — suggests preferred knobs per model family.

marta: thanks all — will update with results.
